title: Emails at a Domain
statement:
Find the users whose email address is at the `example.com` domain. People type their emails in all sorts of letter cases, so `Lee@Example.COM` counts too.

The `users` table has these columns:

- `id`: the user's id, a whole number
- `name`: the user's name
- `email`: the user's email address

Return the columns `id`, `name`, and `email` for every user whose email ends with `@example.com`, ignoring letter case. Addresses at other domains, such as `mail.example.com` or `example.com.au`, do not count. Order the rows by `id`.

Expected output:

```text
 id |    name    |        email
----+------------+----------------------
  1 | Priya Shah | priya@example.com
  3 | Lee Morgan | Lee@Example.COM
  6 | Yuki Ito   | YUKI.ITO@EXAMPLE.COM
(3 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES
  ('Priya Shah', 'priya@example.com'),
  ('Tom Becker', 'tom.becker@gmail.com'),
  ('Lee Morgan', 'Lee@Example.COM'),
  ('Ines Duarte', 'ines@mail.example.com'),
  ('Kofi Mensah', 'kofi@example.com.au'),
  ('Yuki Ito', 'YUKI.ITO@EXAMPLE.COM'),
  ('Dana Novak', 'dana@notexample.com');

tests.output:
id |    name    |        email
----+------------+----------------------
  1 | Priya Shah | priya@example.com
  3 | Lee Morgan | Lee@Example.COM
  6 | Yuki Ito   | YUKI.ITO@EXAMPLE.COM
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ('Marco Bianchi', 'marco@eXample.com'), ('Ruth Cohen', 'ruth@example.org');
tests.output:
id |     name      |        email
----+---------------+----------------------
  1 | Priya Shah    | priya@example.com
  3 | Lee Morgan    | Lee@Example.COM
  6 | Yuki Ito      | YUKI.ITO@EXAMPLE.COM
  8 | Marco Bianchi | marco@eXample.com
(4 rows)

id |    name    |        email
----+------------+----------------------
  2 | Tom Becker | tom@example.com
  3 | Lee Morgan | Lee@Example.COM
  6 | Yuki Ito   | YUKI.ITO@EXAMPLE.COM
(3 rows)

tests.stdin: DELETE FROM users WHERE email ILIKE '%example.com';

hints: `%` at the start of a pattern lets anything come before the part you name.
`ILIKE` works like `LIKE` but ignores letter case.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: keep only emails at example.com, in any letter case
SELECT id, name, email
FROM users
ORDER BY id;
sql.solution:
SELECT id, name, email
FROM users
WHERE email ILIKE '%@example.com'
ORDER BY id;
